scope: R183: stage A passes both axes - verdict equivalence and speed

bug1_writeback.symptom: R182 read garbage values above 0x7fff that the kernel could never write
bug1_writeback.diagnosis: sentinel probe showed only 3 of 8 slots were written and the rest held uninitialised bytes
bug1_writeback.cause: SetGlobalBuffer(y+coreIdx,1) but DataCopy wrote 8 ints per core, so the eight cores overwrote each other with uninitialised buffer contents
bug1_writeback.fix: each core owns an aligned 8-int (32 byte) region, zeroed then publishing blockMax in slot 0; output shape coreNum*8 = 64

bug2_alignment.symptom: every small case returned the same constant 0x5209
bug2_alignment.cause: DataCopy and ReduceMax need 32-byte aligned lengths; 2-6 halfs is 4-12 bytes
bug2_alignment.fix: pad to a multiple of 128 halfs with 0x0000, whose magnitude bits are zero so it cannot change a maximum

key_semantic_finding.finding: AscendC ReduceMax propagates NaN (a NaN input yields 0x7e00)
key_semantic_finding.why_it_matters: R165 measured torch's max() masking NaN, which made a plain Abs+ReduceMax look unsafe; the AscendC primitive behaves differently, so the simplest kernel is correct and no bit masking with Ands is needed
key_semantic_finding.unresolved_by_the_fix: Ands is not used at all, so its missing 16-bit instantiation no longer matters

test_bug_found.detail: the hand-rolled C++ f16() truncates instead of round-to-nearest, so f16(65503) gave 0x7bfe instead of 0x7bff
test_bug_found.verdict: the expectation was wrong, not the kernel
test_bug_found.fix: pin the explicit bit patterns, consistent with round180/reference180.py
